to those old enough. what was traffic or work like on 9/11?
Traffic was the same as always. Everyone at work was furious. I was nowhere near NYC though.

I was active duty AF... I don't recall traffic around town being noteworthy, but getting on base was VERY time consuming as they were checking every ID (they didn't use to do that) as well as vehicle checks. At work, we all just sat around the TV watching it all play out, stunned and wondering where we would be deploying to once our inevitable response kicked off.

I was a civilian and working on a contract that needed me to be in a secure envirionment. This took place on a base. I was elsewhere on that day but needed to be there the following day. When I got there, they refused to let me and my employee in.

Outside the base area, traffic was very light. It was as if the world stopped. The strangest thing that I noticed was the lack of planes in the sky. The only planes in the air were military. It was very surreal.

Incidentally, we weren't allowed back on base for about six months, putting the project behind and costing you a bunch of money.

I had just gotten home from a business trip to Europe the day before so I went in late. I woke up, saw what was going on and drove to work very numb. When I got there I told people what was going on and people didn't believe me. Soon after, they sent us all home because we didn't know how big the threat was or who was a target and I worked for a global company that MAY have been a target (again, we had no idea WHO was a target). Traffic was the same but the really weird thing was for the next month or so not a SINGLE airplane was in the sky. I remember the weird feeling when I finally saw an airplane and it felt like ages since I saw one that it was almost foreign to me.

I was the captain on a Medevac jet going to PANC ( anchorage, AK) they said the airport was (closed) no one new what to do. We were escorted from the final approach fix ("BRUCK" if my memory serves me) to runway 6R. I immediately called and woke up my wife. Crazy morning.

No traffic was allowed in lower Manhattan.
Crowds of people were walking in the streets. No panic at all.
Whole city was quiet except for the occasional siren.
The strench from the fire was everywhere. Burning plastic metalic smell stayed for 2 weeks.
Subways stopped running for most of the day atleast the ones going to lower Manhattan.

Work:
Got to work and someone mentioned a plane had hit one of the twin towers.
Thought no big deal. Probably a small prop plane hit the tower.
In the office, we had a open seating/desk format. About 15-20 of us all together in 40x60 area.
Sitting down at my desk, one of my co-workers announced,"a second plane hit the other tower."
Everyone stopped moving. Hard swallow followed. A deliberate attack. This is fucked. Real bad.
Everyone started calling friends and family.
The reservist in the group just got up and left. Some left work immediately.
Others stuck around. Those that stuck around were glued to cable news.
Late in the afternoon. I walked mid town to Brooklyn.
Cell service was absolute shit. All lines were jammed.
A saw a police car heading up town with about a foot of gray powder( reminded me of thick insulation) covering the whole car except the windows. Not healthy atmosphere. Didn't stay downtown long.

A really good friend was working in the towers.
Cause she was such a slacker, she was really late to work. Being late saved her life.

Everyone was concerned about friends and family. Lost an ex-coworker that day.
No looting. No conflict.
City was reeling in pain and no one wanted to cause anymore.

It's actually kind of impossible to describe to someone who hasn't gone through anything similar.

Traffic slowed to a trickle as the day went on, and what there was felt surreal because of the shock of what had happened.

Work was... Imagine everybody at your job acting like they were afraid somebody they knew had just died, but had no way to check to find out for sure. Quiet. Tense. And then the one guy who works a later shift, slept through his alarm, and hadn't paused to check news or listen to the radio bursts in loudly, cheerful as hell, and everybody just Looks at him.

Remember, we had no fucking idea who had done it for a couple of days, or why it was done. We just knew, for certain, that we'd all been attacked.
